lines.text: What would happen to planet Earth if our atmosphere suddenly lost half of its air pressure?
Instantly, sea level air would feel as thin as the death zone summit of Mount Everest.
Every human on the planet would gasp for oxygen, losing consciousness within two minutes from acute hypoxia.
Water would boil at just one hundred and fifty degrees Fahrenheit, making hot cooking impossible.
With less atmospheric shielding, lethal ultraviolet solar radiation and meteors would bombard the ground unchecked.
Sky color would darken from brilliant azure blue to an eerie dark indigo even at midday.
Our thick blanket of air is the only shield protecting us from the hostile void of space.
